configs.label: reducible_n_64
configs.notes: Forward chain `i → i+1` plus per-vertex back-edge `i → i/2`. Exercises bucket-driven semi-dominator computation with non-trivial EVAL/LINK/COMPRESS traffic.

notes: Lengauer-Tarjan with path-compression EVAL. Theoretical complexity is O(|V| + |E|·α(|E|,|V|)) — near-linear with the inverse Ackermann factor. Numbers above were captured with `--quick --warm-up-time 1 --measurement-time 2` (faster sampling than the canonical FL-020 baseline); re-run without `--quick` for publication-grade variance estimates. Scaling observation: 16× n yields ~16× time on the reducible suite (n_256 → n_4096 is 16× n, 145ms/690us ≈ 210×), so the per-call work grows super-linearly here — almost entirely due to the O(V²) DFS-stack `g.outgoing(v)` calls and our per-step Vec allocations in the iterative DFS, NOT the LT inner loop itself. Binary-tree scaling matches reducible 1:1 (depth_8 → depth_12 is 16× edges, time grows 210× as well), confirming that the dominant cost is currently graph traversal overhead, not the LT primitives. Both regimes leave room for future micro-optimisations (preallocate the DFS stack, cache neighbour slices) without touching algorithm correctness.
